summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science background: asymptotic analysis of algorithms and solving simple cost recurrences, basic Turing machines and multitape simulation, binary representation of integers and machine arithmetic (carries, two's complement, XOR, fixed-point rounding), and the discrete mathematics taught to everyone (induction, modular arithmetic, gcd, primes, the Chinese remainder theorem, permutations, binomial coefficients, lexicographic order). From the required mathematics they have a first course in linear algebra (vectors, matrices, rank, invertibility, triangular and diagonal matrices, linear maps over Q and C) and basic complex numbers and polynomials. They have not studied tensor products of operators, bilinear forms, Hadamard or Bruhat-type factorizations, FFT variants beyond a textbook mention, or research-level integer multiplication algorithms.

known.name: Binary representation of integers
known.gloss: Writing a nonnegative integer as a sum of distinct powers of two, recorded as a string of bits, with an n-bit integer lying below 2^n.

known.name: Carry propagation
known.gloss: The schoolbook rule for adding numbers in positional notation, where any digit sum at least the radix passes its excess as a carry into the next position.

known.name: Two's complement
known.gloss: The representation of signed integers in w bits in which a negative x is stored as 2^w + x, so the top bit acts as the sign.

known.name: Exclusive or
known.gloss: The bit operation returning 1 exactly when its two inputs differ, equal to addition modulo 2 and its own inverse.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication
known.gloss: Multiplying two n-digit numbers by summing shifted partial products, which costs O(n^2) digit operations.

known.name: Floor and ceiling
known.gloss: The largest integer at most x and the smallest integer at least x, respectively.

known.name: Rounding to the nearest integer
known.gloss: Replacing a real number by an integer close to it, so that a value known to within less than 1/2 of an integer determines that integer exactly.

known.name: Fixed-point numbers
known.gloss: Storing a real number as an integer times a fixed power of two, so a fixed number of bits sits after the binary point.

known.name: Binary logarithm
known.gloss: The exponent to which 2 must be raised to give x, written lg x, with other bases differing only by a constant factor inside big-O.

known.name: Modular arithmetic
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers where two numbers are identified when their difference is divisible by a fixed modulus m.

known.name: Greatest common divisor
known.gloss: The largest integer dividing both of two integers, with the integers called coprime when it equals 1.

known.name: Prime numbers
known.gloss: Integers greater than 1 whose only positive divisors are 1 and themselves, from which every positive integer is uniquely a product.

known.name: Chinese remainder theorem
known.gloss: For pairwise coprime moduli s_1, …, s_d, the map sending an integer modulo their product to its tuple of residues is a bijection.

known.name: Mathematical induction
known.gloss: Proving a statement for all natural numbers by proving a base case and that each case implies the next.

known.name: Recurrence relations for running time
known.gloss: Inequalities bounding an algorithm's cost on size n by its cost on smaller sizes plus extra work, solved by unrolling or the master method.

known.name: Geometric series
known.gloss: A sum of terms with a constant ratio r, which for |r| < 1 is bounded by the first term divided by 1 − r.

known.name: Permutations
known.gloss: Bijections of a finite set to itself, used to reorder the entries of a sequence and composable and invertible.

known.name: Binomial coefficients
known.gloss: The number C(n, k) of k-element subsets of an n-element set.

known.name: Lexicographic order
known.gloss: Ordering tuples by their first coordinate, breaking ties by the second, and so on.

known.name: Vectors and matrices
known.gloss: Rectangular arrays of numbers representing linear maps between coordinate spaces, multiplied by composing those maps.

known.name: Vector spaces, subspaces and dimension
known.gloss: Sets closed under addition and scalar multiplication, with dimension the size of any basis, and linear maps the functions respecting both operations.

known.name: Matrix rank
known.gloss: The dimension of the column space of a matrix, equal to the maximum number of linearly independent rows or columns.

known.name: Invertible matrices
known.gloss: Square matrices with a two-sided inverse, equivalently with nonzero determinant or full rank.

known.name: Triangular and diagonal matrices
known.gloss: Square matrices whose entries above (lower triangular) or off (diagonal) the main diagonal are zero.

known.name: Permutation matrices
known.gloss: 0–1 matrices with exactly one 1 in each row and column, which reorder the coordinates of a vector.

known.name: Gaussian elimination
known.gloss: Reducing a matrix by elementary row and column operations to compute its rank, inverse or a triangular factorization.

known.name: Rational numbers
known.gloss: Numbers p/q with integers p and q ≠ 0, forming a field over which matrices can be manipulated exactly.

known.name: Maximum norm
known.gloss: The largest absolute value of the entries of a vector, used to bound sizes and errors coordinatewise.

known.name: Triangle inequality
known.gloss: The bound saying the size of a sum is at most the sum of the sizes, used to add up error contributions.

known.name: Exponential function and Euler's formula
known.gloss: The exponential e^x, extended to complex arguments by e^{iθ} = cos θ + i sin θ, giving points on the unit circle.
